Simulated ground-truth data for time-varying vaccine effectiveness

Source: R/data.R
ve_sim.Rd

Two scenarios simulated with the HERMES individual-based model (waning-VE extension) in which the true vaccine effectiveness as a function of time since vaccination, VE(t), is known. Both use the same synthetic population of 10,000 people, a slowed influenza-like epidemic over 180 days, and a rolling vaccination campaign (16 ten-day rounds from day 21, each vaccinating 3% of the remaining eligible population). They differ only in the VE curve:

Usage

ve_sim_waning

ve_sim_no_waning

Format

Each is a list with elements:

demographic

Data frame, one row per individual: ind_id, age, sex, hh_id, classroom_id, workplace_id.

vaccination

Data frame, one row per vaccinated individual: ind_id, time_of_vaccination (study day).

incidence

Data frame, one row per reported case: ind_id, time_of_reporting (study day; includes a reporting delay, so can exceed study_end). About 10% of symptomatic cases are unreported.

params

List of HERMES parameters used. The true VE(t) is defined by vaccine_effectiveness (peak), ve_ramp_days, ve_half_life and ve_floor.

study_end

Length of the study in days (180).

hermes_commit

Commit of ibm_hermes that generated the data.

An object of class list of length 6.

An object of class list of length 6.

Source

Generated by data-raw/ve_test_scenarios.R using https://github.com/kylieainslie/ibm_hermes (branch waning-vaccine-effectiveness).

Details

  • ve_sim_waning: VE rises linearly to 0.8 over 14 days, then decays exponentially (half-life 45 days) towards a floor of 0.1.

  • ve_sim_no_waning: VE rises linearly to 0.8 over 14 days, then stays at 0.8.

The two runs are not paired realisations of one epidemic: transmission is random and diverges between them from the start.

Some vaccinated individuals were reported as cases before their vaccination date, because HERMES vaccinates from the whole eligible population, including people already infected.
